description: Quiescence search keeps the search horizon from cutting a line in the middle of an exchange. Where alpha-beta runs out of depth, it does not trust the evaluation of a position that still has *noisy* moves, such as captures; it searches those moves alone, ply after ply, until none is left. At each such position the side to move may *stand pat*: decline every noisy move and keep the position's evaluation, which becomes the score to beat. A game opts in by listing its noisy moves in `Game::noisy_moves`; minimax, negamax, alpha-beta, PVS and MTD(f) then all search past the horizon, and quiescence positions stay out of the transposition table. Each noisy move must bring the game closer to a quiet position, as a capture removes a piece, or the search never ends.

papers.title: Programming a computer for playing chess
papers.venue: The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science
